setlist.title: Goin' Down The Road Feeling Bad

liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **Candyman** (3 reviews): Starts a run through Passenger where the band is full-on and rocking, after an ordinary Sugaree and El Paso; Reviewer loves the Garcia solo in this song [9][11][13]
- **From The Heart Of Me** (2 reviews): Excellent version, with Donna in strong form; Recording captures the luxurious quality of Donna's voice, which adds beauty to the band's sound [10][13]
- **Loser** (1 review): Described as smoldering [11]
- **Ship Of Fools** (1 review): Reviewer thinks this may be one of the best versions of the song [8]
- **Estimated Prophet** (1 review): Played with Eyes of the World as top-notch versions that lift the second set [9]
- **Not Fade Away** (1 review): Raucous run into Goin' Down the Road and Johnny B. Goode that likely had everyone on their feet [9]
- **Goin' Down The Road Feeling Bad** (1 review): Garcia plays in overdrive and lets loose, notably in a turnaround just after four minutes [8]

## The recordings

- **gd1978-11-14.nak300.rolfe.miller.100205.sbeok.flac16** (recommended): source not stated; 20 songs; 163 min; rated 4.62/5 by 13 [1]. Said about its sound: Reviewer says the Rolfe master sounds very good and conveys the crowd's excitement from the opening; Superior audience recording that captures the crowd's excitement without fan interference; vocals and harmonies come through well [6][10]
- **gd78-11-14.sony.11485.sbeok.shnf**: audience recording; 20 songs; 144 min; rated 3.83/5 by 6 [2]. Said about its sound: Reviewer finds the audience recording's quality excellent [3]

## Around the show

- Reviewer attended the show and remembers its frenetic energy; had seen over a dozen Dead/JGB shows [3]
- First Dead show for the reviewer, who bought the last four tickets at Montgomery Wards' Ticketron for $9.50 each after Styx sold out [4]
- Crowd is clearly into it, feeding off the energy; Donna is audible and not drowned out [11]
- Reviewer finds the jamming restrained, not a wildly experimental, record-setting night compared with the band's most adventurous shows [7]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd1978-11-14.nak300.rolfe.miller.100205.sbeok.flac16**: taped by Steve Rolfe; transferred by Charlie Miller; source: Nakamichi 300/CP1 -> Cassette Master (Maxell UDXLI/Dolby B) [1]. Also: Steve's master tape surfaced after more than twenty years in a closet; Recorded by Steve Rolfe from front row center of the balcony; the uploader was lent his masters [1][6]
- **gd78-11-14.sony.11485.sbeok.shnf**: source: Audience Recording: Sony ECM-280's [2]. Also: Audience recording on Sony ECM-280 microphones, then MC, DAT and CDR; seeded to etree by T. Wiley [2]
